scenes.say: Why does dot net start up so quickly, yet keep running fast? Let’s break down tiered compilation.

scenes.label: Tiered
scenes.sub: First, compile methods fast. Later, recompile hot code with optimizations.
scenes.say: Tiered compilation means the just-in-time compiler first compiles methods quickly for a fast startup. Later, it recompiles hot code with more optimizations.
Here’s how it works: The JIT quickly compiles methods so your app starts fast. As some methods get used more, the runtime spots them and recompiles those with extra optimizations.

scenes.title: Tiered Compilation Enabled
scenes.say: In dot net seven, tiered compilation is on by default. This helps both startup and steady-state performance.

scenes.question: Does tiered compilation slow startup?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it adds overhead up front.
scenes.right: No, it speeds up startup by compiling quickly first, then optimizes later.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: Does tiered compilation slow down startup? Nope. It actually speeds things up by compiling quickly first, then optimizing hot code as your app runs.
